_comment: Friendly-to-real name mapping for penny-mcp's schema. The LLM sees/writes ONLY friendly names; sql_translator.py swaps them before SQL execution; result_sanitizer.py uses the reverse mapping to hide real names from LLM-visible data. Built from E:\realbooks\realbooks-penny-mcp\app\resources\schema.py's real schema (six tables), reusing realbooks-agents' friendly vocabulary where the underlying column matches.

Transactions.description: Financial transactions — income, expenses, refunds, and loan payments

Properties.description: Properties the user owns or manages

Loans.description: Mortgages and loans linked to properties

Projects.description: Renovation projects and rooms linked to properties. Main projects have no ParentProjectId; rooms/sub-projects have ParentProjectId set to their parent's Id.

CategoryLookup.description: Maps category IDs to human-readable category names (e.g. Rent, Insurance, Loan Payment)

sql_rules.money: Income uses income-type amounts, expenses use expense-type amounts. Net is income minus expenses. Refunds are tracked separately.
sql_rules.split_transactions: Split-child rows are automatically excluded by mandatory filters — you never need to filter for this yourself.
sql_rules.loan_payment_breakdown: Loan payments have LoanId set. Use PrincipalPaid, InterestPaid, EscrowPaid, PMIPaid, LateFees for breakdowns only. For totals, use Amount.
sql_rules.projects_vs_rooms: Projects with no ParentProjectId are main projects; rows with ParentProjectId set are rooms/sub-projects of that project.

tool_description_rewrites.execute_query:
Execute a read-only SQL query against the RealBooks database and return up to 200 rows as JSON. Use this for ad-hoc or cross-resource data listings: properties, entities, transactions, projects, loans, or any combination.
Write your SQL using ONLY the friendly table/column names from the data catalog in your system prompt — the translator converts them to the database names automatically before execution and adds the mandatory filters (account scoping, soft-delete, archive, split-transaction) for you. You never write those filters yourself, and you never pass an account id — it is applied automatically.
SELECT only — INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, DROP, and TRUNCATE are rejected.
tool_description_rewrites.generate_report:
Generate a visual financial report from a SELECT query and return it to the user. The chart renders automatically on the frontend — never add links, URLs, or image tags.
viz_type (default 'auto' picks for you): 'line' for time series/monthly trends, 'bar' for comparisons across properties/entities or income-vs-expense, 'pie' for a category breakdown of <=8 groups, 'scalar' for a single total/KPI. Never use 'table' — always aggregate and chart.
Write your SQL using ONLY the friendly table/column names from the data catalog in your system prompt — the translator converts them to the database names automatically before execution and adds the mandatory filters (account scoping, soft-delete, archive, split-transaction) for you. You never pass an account id — it is applied automatically.
Returns {"status": "no_data"} when the query matches 0 rows — when you see this, tell the user in plain text (e.g. 'No expenses found for that property') and do NOT retry. You never need to run a separate COUNT first; this tool detects empty results for you.
